home.welcomeBody: New here? Learn everything about TBTs on the {roast}. And set up your {profile} as a creator, collector, or both — it’s used whenever you create or acquire a TBT, and it appears on the work’s page.

sections.roastNote: Roast — learn everything about TBTs. What a Transferable Billable Token is, how certification works, royalties, and verification. The onboarding surface, in the spirit of an “NFT 101.”
sections.grindNote: Grind — the discovery floor. Browse, curate, share, and compare TBTs. (The Charts live here.)
sections.brewNote: Brew — where a creator makes a TBT: upload the work, set price and royalties, and certify it on-chain. The first TBT auto-creates “Series 1.”

brew.registeredBodyFull: Your work is permanently on-chain. Your certificate — with your private transfer key — has been sent to your phone.
brew.certKeyInside: Your transfer key is inside — kept private, off this screen.
brew.verifyOnChainNote: Opens your record in the Solana block explorer
brew.sealBiometricNote: Seal with a single touch next time.
brew.feedPending: Not connected yet — add a line yourself if you want it on the record.
brew.tipValue: A figure is suggested so you have a starting point, but it is written into the certificate and the royalty terms travel with the work on every future sale — so confirm it rather than accepting it. If the work is not for sale, set the price to zero and royalties to none.
brew.tipRoyalty: A share of future resales that returns to you automatically each time the work changes hands. Choose a percentage or a fixed amount.
brew.tipProtection: Before a work is certified we compare its image against every work already registered on TBT and against public sources on the open web. A clean result strengthens your claim. If something similar exists, you decide how to declare the relationship — your own work, a derivative, or an authorised edition — and that declaration travels with the certificate.
brew.tipMoment: These anchors are captured automatically from your location and the world today, then written into the certificate. Because they become part of a permanent record, read them before you continue — every line can be edited, and anything you would rather not publish can be removed.
brew.visionSub: Record a short piece about the work — it becomes part of the authenticity record.
brew.visionHint: Tap to record · up to 1 minute · audio or video
brew.imageEmptyHint: Take a photo or choose a file below
brew.tipAssetAnchors: Links to where your work lives online — a YouTube video, a Drive folder, an IPFS hash, a portfolio page. They anchor the certificate to the real files.
brew.tipDimensions: The size of the work in its own terms — cm or inches for physical pieces, pixels or resolution for digital, duration for time-based work.
brew.tipSeries: A series groups your own work — a body of pieces that belong together. Every work belongs to one. If you haven’t made a series yet, this one starts Series 1, which you can rename at any time.
brew.gateBody: To brew a TBT you need a Creator Profile — the identity that appears on every certificate.
